hook: Binding a cofactor to iron cuts the barrier for O2 activation by 12.7 kcal/mol, a 10^10 rate boost.

readout.label: Lower barrier for peroxo formation from pterin binding

summary: In tryptophan hydroxylase, the pterin cofactor binding to iron lowers the barrier to form the key peroxo intermediate by 12.7 kcal per mol, roughly ten billion times faster. The team used stable nitric oxide as a stand-in for the unobservable oxygen species, read with several spectroscopies. The oxygen result is extrapolated from that analog.
title: Role of (Co)substrate Coordination to Iron in Activating Its Two-Electron Reduction of Dioxygen: Mechanism of Pterin Activation in Tryptophan Hydroxylase
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
